title: Divisors and rationally trivialized lines on a regular algebraic space
statement:
Let $X$ be a regular Noetherian separated algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Here regular means that every scheme etale over $X$ is regular; Noetherian means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally Noetherian, and separated means that the diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is a closed immersion. A Weil divisor is a finite integral linear combination of integral closed subspaces of codimension one, with codimension computed on etale scheme charts. A Cartier divisor is a section of $\mathcal K_X^\times/\mathcal O_X^\times$, where $\mathcal K_X$ is the sheaf of total quotient rings on the small etale site. A nonzero rational section of a line module means a generator at each generic point of each irreducible component, or equivalently a generator after tensoring with $\mathcal K_X$.

Cartier divisors and Weil divisors on $X$ are canonically identified. Every line module $L$ on $X$ admits a nonzero rational section $s$. Its divisor $\operatorname{div}(s)$ is the sum of its orders at codimension-one points, computed in etale charts using the normalized valuation of the local discrete valuation ring. For every Weil divisor $D$ there is a line module $\mathcal O_X(D)$ with a canonical nonzero rational section $s_D$ of divisor $D$. Explicitly, on an etale scheme chart where the Cartier divisor of $D$ is the class of a local section $f$ of $\mathcal K_X^\times$, $\mathcal O_X(D)=f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\subseteq\mathcal K_X$ and $s_D=1$. Every pair $(L,s)$ has a unique isomorphism $(L,s)\simeq(\mathcal O_X(\operatorname{div}(s)),s_{\operatorname{div}(s)})$ preserving the rational sections. A rational section $s$ extends to an everywhere generating regular section if and only if $\operatorname{div}(s)=0$. Two maps between line modules equal on a dense open are equal. These identifications respect restriction to open subspaces, and the associated line modules and sections respect etale pullback. More generally, let $q:X'\to X$ be a flat morphism (flat on etale scheme charts) [def-weil-flat-morphism] to $X$ from another regular Noetherian separated algebraic space $X'$. Pulling back local equations defines the Cartier pullback $q^*D$ of every Weil divisor $D$ of $X$, the pullback $q^*s$ of a nonzero rational section is a nonzero rational section, and there is a unique isomorphism $q^*(\mathcal O_X(D),s_D)\simeq(\mathcal O_{X'}(q^*D),s_{q^*D})$ preserving the rational sections; consequently $\operatorname{div}(q^*s)=q^*\operatorname{div}(s)$. On a scheme, line modules here are the usual invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module].

proof.text: Apply the meromorphic generic-chart model to $X$ and $L$. Each $L_\eta$ is a one-dimensional vector space over $k(\eta)$; choose a basis $s_\eta$. The tuple $(s_\eta)_\eta$ is a global section of $\mathcal K_X(L)$ and generates it over $\mathcal K_X$, since componentwise multiplication by a nonzero basis coordinate is invertible. This gives the asserted nonzero rational section, also when $X$ is disconnected; for the empty space the tuple is empty. Throughout, use connected affine etale charts, whose rings are Noetherian normal domains, and interpret line modules on scheme charts by the ordinary-to-etale equivalence.

A Cartier section is represented on an etale covering by invertible meromorphic functions $f_i$, with $f_i/f_j$ a regular unit on overlaps. On a connected normal affine chart, the principal-divisor kernel lemma gives a finite cycle of normalized codimension-one orders; it is additive on multiplication and vanishes on units. The cycle-descent lemma identifies these cycles under further etale restriction and descends them to a unique Weil divisor on $X$. Local finiteness is finite support here: choose a finite covering of the quasi-compact $X$ by affine charts with local equations; the finite union of their finite order supports has finite image. If two Cartier sections have the same Weil divisor, their ratio on any connected affine refinement has zero principal divisor. The kernel lemma says this ratio is a regular unit. The local classes in $\mathcal K_X^\times/\mathcal O_X^\times$ therefore agree; its sheaf axiom gives equality globally. This proves injectivity and also makes the order convention unambiguous.

Conversely, pull a Weil divisor $E$ back to a quasi-compact etale scheme atlas $U$ by cycle descent. Work on a connected affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $U$: by the model, $R$ is a Noetherian normal domain, and it is regular. Fix a point $x$ with prime $\mathfrak q$; discard the finitely many prime divisors of $E$ on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ not containing $x$ (remove their union), and let $J_a$ be the primes of the remaining ones, with coefficients $n_a\in\mathbf Z$. For the Cartier equations $f_i$ of $E$, form $M_i=f_i^{-1}\mathcal O_{U_i}\subset\mathcal K_{U_i}$. Each is a free line with basis $f_i^{-1}$. If $f_i/f_j$ is a unit, these are equal submodules of the meromorphic sheaf on the overlap; their identification is the identity on rational elements and satisfies the triple-overlap cocycle. Etale descent of line modules gives $\mathcal O_X(E)$; its local injections into $\mathcal K_X$ agree, so the sheaf axiom realizes it as the subsheaf given by these $M_i$. In its meromorphic localization, the element $1$ agrees on all overlaps and is a generator. Set $s_E=1$. Relative to $f_i^{-1}$ its coefficient is $f_i$, so Step 2 gives $\operatorname{div}(s_E)=E$. These formulas give the explicit construction in the statement, including negative coefficients.

proof.text: For any rationally trivialized line $(L,s)$, choose local frames $e_i$ on scheme charts and write $s=g_i e_i$ with $g_i\in\mathcal K^\times$. A change of frame multiplies $g_i$ by a regular unit, so its orders define $E=\operatorname{div}(s)$ by Steps 2 and 3. The map $g_i^{-1}\mathcal O\to L$, $a\mapsto a g_i e_i$, is a regular isomorphism: it sends the basis $g_i^{-1}$ to $e_i$. It sends the rational section $1$ to $s$. On overlaps both maps send every rational scalar $a$ to $as$, so they agree by the injective meromorphic embedding of a line. Full faithfulness in etale descent glues them to $\mathcal O_X(E)\simeq L$. A second such isomorphism has the same meromorphic map, since $1$ generates after meromorphic localization; injectivity of $L\to\mathcal K_X(L)$ makes it equal to the first. Invert this unique isomorphism to obtain the orientation in the statement.

proof.text: In the same frame $s=g_i e_i$, it extends to a regular generating section exactly when $g_i$ is a regular unit. By the principal-divisor kernel lemma on connected normal affine refinements, this holds exactly when all codimension-one orders of $g_i$ vanish. The extension glues uniquely, since its images in the meromorphic sheaf agree. Therefore $s$ is everywhere generating if and only if $\operatorname{div}(s)=0$. This tests the given rational section, rather than just the isomorphism class of its line.

Let $a,b:L\to M$ agree on a dense open $W$. Apply the generic-chart model to the line $L^\vee\otimes M$: in local frames its regular sections are exactly the coefficients of maps $L\to M$. The coefficient of $a-b$ restricts to zero on $W$, hence is zero by the dense-open injection of that model. Thus $a=b$. Open restriction and further etale restriction preserve the equations $f_i$, the submodules $f_i^{-1}\mathcal O$, and the maps $a\mapsto as$ above, by the meromorphic chart model. Consequently all the identifications commute with these restrictions. On schemes the ordinary-to-etale equivalence identifies these lines with the usual invertible modules.

For the flat $q:X'\to X$, use the enlarged ringed-etale-site model to compute module pullback as tensor inverse image. After choosing charts of $X$ and refining their inverse images by affine charts of $X'$, the calculation is a flat ring map $A\to A'$ of reduced rings. The total-fraction comparison lemma states that non-zero-divisors of $A$ map to non-zero-divisors of $A'$ and gives the map $Q(A)\to Q(A')$, $a/t\mapsto q(a)/q(t)$. Only this first assertion of that lemma is used (its finite intermediate algebra may be taken to be $A$). Hence every local equation $f_i\in Q(A)^\times$ pulls back to $q(f_i)\in Q(A')^\times$; regular-unit ratios remain units. These equations define a Cartier divisor, hence by Steps 2 and 3 a Weil divisor $q^*E$ on $X'$. No flat cycle pullback with a relative dimension assumption is used.

Locally $q^*(f_i^{-1}\mathcal O)$ is free with basis $1\otimes f_i^{-1}$, and $1\otimes f_i^{-1}\mapsto q(f_i)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism to $q(f_i)^{-1}\mathcal O_{X'}$. The rational element $1=f_i f_i^{-1}$ maps to $q(f_i)q(f_i)^{-1}=1$. The transition ratios are the images of the original ratios, so these local isomorphisms glue. Likewise $s=g_i e_i$ pulls back to $q(g_i)q^*e_i$, which is a generator over the meromorphic sheaf since $q(g_i)$ is a unit there. Its divisor is the Weil divisor represented by the Cartier equations $q(g_i)$, exactly $q^*\operatorname{div}(s)$ by Step 8. This proves the asserted pullback identity and the isomorphism of pairs; its uniqueness follows as in Step 5 from the injective meromorphic embedding on $X'$.
